podcast_name: Best of the Best in Franchising
episode_title: Interview with Frank Fiume, Founder of i9 Sports and Host of the Emerging Brands Podcast
question: How did i9 Sports grow from a startup to 4 million participants across 41 states with over $400 million in revenue?
transcript_excerpt: i9 Sports experienced a 15 to 20 year overnight success. The company lost $850,000 in the first two years but Frank Fiume made critical changes including hiring better staff, converting training and support systems, and refining franchisee selection criteria. By 2006-2007, they hit their 100th franchise location within four years, positioning the company to survive the 2008-2009 recession with minimal problems through strict financial standards for franchisee qualification.

podcast_name: Best of the Best in Franchising
episode_title: Interview with Frank Fiume, Founder of i9 Sports and Host of the Emerging Brands Podcast
question: Why did i9 Sports transition from adult and kids sports to exclusively kids sports in 2003-2005?
transcript_excerpt: Frank Fiume quickly found out within the first two years that he could not replicate his success of adult sports with franchisees like he had done in New York. Changing i9 Sports to be strictly for kids proved to be a blessing in disguise because the brand became much more targeted, they knew their audience, and they knew how to market it effectively.

question: What does the name i9 Sports stand for and how was it created?
transcript_excerpt: The name i9 Sports comes from words Frank Fiume wanted his company to embody: integrity, imaginative, innovative, insightful, instructional, and passion. He created the name by writing down all the words symbolic for the company and noticed a whole bunch of I words, then realized i to the ninth power looked incredibly unique and powerful. The name was chosen specifically because it was unique, trademarkable, and easy to protect legally, though it required more marketing investment because it was not descriptive.

episode_title: Interview with Frank Fiume, Founder of i9 Sports and Host of the Emerging Brands Podcast
question: What is the entrepreneur identity crisis described in Frank Fiume's book Running With My Head Down?
transcript_excerpt: The entrepreneur identity crisis occurs when founders breathe, eat, drink, and sleep their business so completely that they and their business become one and the same. Frank Fiume overcame this at a Tony Robbins Date with Destiny event in 2008 when he realized that to give his company what it needed, he had to separate his identity from the business and say out loud: I am more than i9 Sports and i9 Sports is more than me. This separation allowed him to see the business objectively and helped it really explode.

episode_title: Interview with Frank Fiume, Founder of i9 Sports and Host of the Emerging Brands Podcast
question: How did Frank Fiume overcome lonely at the top syndrome as i9 Sports grew?
transcript_excerpt: Frank Fiume found that as the company grew, he could no longer be friends with employees and had to transition to being the boss. He could not freely share his ideas because they would impact people's jobs. To overcome this loneliness at the top, he sought outside organizations and peer networking groups such as Entrepreneur Organization, YPO, or Vistage that allowed him to talk with other founders and entrepreneurs about their challenges.
